summary: This resolution removes Rep. Tony Gonzales of Texas from the House Appropriations and Homeland Security committees.

scores.thoughts: The resolution removes a single Member from the Appropriations Committee but does not alter any spending levels, programs, or policies. Committee membership changes have no direct effect on government spending.
The bill addresses only House committee assignments and contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, or enforcement.
No provisions in the resolution concern healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
The resolution is silent on firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration-related content appears in the bill text.
The resolution does not address reproductive rights or abortion policy.
Although the Member is removed from Appropriations (which funds defense), the resolution itself makes no change to defense spending levels or policy.
No environmental or climate provisions are present.
The bill does not modify any welfare, entitlement, or social safety-net programs.
No education policy, funding, or school-choice provisions are included.
The resolution contains nothing related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
While the preamble references conduct rules, the measure does not alter criminal sentencing, policing, or justice-system policy.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions exist in the text.
Committee assignment changes do not affect deficit or debt-reduction policy.
The resolution does not address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
Although Appropriations handles foreign aid, the bill makes no substantive change to aid levels or policy.
No voting access, election integrity, or electoral reform measures are present.
The bill contains no technology, data-privacy, or regulatory provisions.
No labor, union, or worker-protection content appears.
The resolution does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination policy.
